A thermoelectric conversion module includes a thermoelectric conversion module body and a heat transfer portion. The thermoelectric conversion module body includes a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates, each comprising a flexible insulating substrate having, on one surface thereof, at least one of: (i) a P-type thermoelectric conversion element comprising a P-type thermoelectric conversion layer and a pair of connection electrodes electrically connected thereto; or (ii) an N-type thermoelectric conversion element comprising an N-type thermoelectric conversion layer and a pair of connection electrodes electrically connected thereto. The thermoelectric conversion module substrates are arranged such that the direction of the connection electrodes is aligned with the direction of the insulating substrates.

The heat transfer portion is provided on a side of the thermoelectric conversion module body proximate to at least one connection electrode of each thermoelectric conversion module substrate. The heat transfer portion presses the thermoelectric conversion module substrates in the arrangement direction and either transfers heat to the thermoelectric conversion module body or dissipates heat therefrom. The heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of 10 W/mK or higher. When the thermoelectric conversion module substrates are pressed in the arrangement direction by the heat transfer portion, the normal stress in a direction perpendicular to the surface of each insulating substrate is 0.01 MPa or higher.

A thermoelectric conversion module comprises a module body and a heat-transfer section. The module body is formed from multiple thermoelectric conversion module substrates. Each substrate includes a flexible insulating substrate having, on one surface, at least one of the following: (i) a P-type thermoelectric conversion element containing a P-type thermoelectric conversion layer and two connection electrodes electrically coupled to that layer, or (ii) an N-type thermoelectric conversion element containing an N-type thermoelectric conversion layer and two connection electrodes electrically coupled to that layer. When the substrates are pressed in the arrangement direction by the heat-transfer section, the resulting normal stress perpendicular to the surface of each insulating substrate is at least 0.01 MPa.

The thermoelectric conversion module includes a module body formed from a plurality of thermoelectric conversion module substrates. Each substrate comprises a flexible insulating substrate carrying at least one P-type or N-type thermoelectric conversion element. Each thermoelectric conversion element includes a thermoelectric layer and a pair of electrodes electrically connected to the thermoelectric layer.

The substrates are arranged such that the direction in which the paired electrodes are connected is aligned with the arrangement direction of the insulating substrates. A heat transfer portion presses the substrates along this arrangement direction and is configured either to supply heat to the module body or to dissipate heat from it. To ensure effective heat transfer and reliable contact, the heat transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK and applies a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa perpendicular to the substrates.
outputs.L4:
A thermoelectric conversion module includes a plurality of flexible insulating substrates on which P-type thermoelectric conversion elements, N-type thermoelectric conversion elements, or both are provided. The substrates are arranged in alignment so that the thermoelectric elements form a prescribed electrical connection and are positioned between regions having different temperatures. Depending on the desired configuration, the P-type and N-type elements may be arranged alternately and connected electrically in series while being thermally coupled in parallel. The flexibility of the insulating substrates allows the module to conform to uneven, curved, or dimensionally varying surfaces.

A heat-transfer portion is disposed in contact with the aligned substrates. The heat-transfer portion supplies heat to the thermoelectric elements, dissipates heat from the elements, or performs both functions on opposite sides of the module. It also compresses the substrates in a direction normal to their principal surfaces. The heat-transfer portion has a thermal conductivity of at least 10 W/mK and applies a normal stress of at least 0.01 MPa to the substrates.

The applied pressure reduces gaps and thermal contact resistance between the heat-transfer portion, the flexible substrates, and the thermoelectric elements. At the same time, the relatively high thermal conductivity of the heat-transfer portion promotes rapid and uniform transfer of heat. These characteristics help establish and maintain a temperature difference across the thermoelectric elements, even when the module is mounted on a nonplanar surface or is subjected to dimensional changes during operation.

When a temperature difference is applied, the P-type and N-type elements generate an electromotive force through the Seebeck effect, and the resulting electrical energy can be collected through conductors connected to the elements. Alternatively, when electrical current is supplied to the module, heat can be transferred by the Peltier effect to provide heating or cooling. By combining flexible supporting substrates with a thermally conductive, pressure-applying heat-transfer portion, the module achieves stable thermal contact, reduced heat-transfer loss, and efficient thermoelectric conversion.
outputs.L5:
## MPa: A Unit of Pressure and Stress

**MPa** stands for **megapascal**, a metric unit used to measure pressure, stress, and material strength. One megapascal equals **one million pascals (Pa)**:

**1 MPa = 1,000,000 Pa = 1 N/mm²**

MPa is commonly used in engineering, construction, manufacturing, and materials science. For example, the compressive strength of concrete is often expressed in MPa. Standard structural concrete may have a strength of about 20–40 MPa, while high-strength concrete can exceed 60 MPa. The tensile strength and yield strength of metals are also frequently stated in MPa.

The unit can also describe fluid pressure. Useful conversions include:

- **1 MPa = 10 bar**
- **1 MPa ≈ 145 psi**
- **0.1 MPa ≈ atmospheric pressure at sea level**

Because it is part of the International System of Units (SI), MPa provides a convenient and standardized way to compare pressures and material properties across technical fields.

## Exemplary Patent Language

### Title

**Thermoelectric Conversion Module Including Flexible Insulating Substrates**

### Abstract

A thermoelectric conversion module includes a plurality of flexible insulating substrates, a plurality of thermoelectric elements, and at least one thermally conductive member. Each thermoelectric element is of a P-type or an N-type and is disposed on a corresponding one of the flexible insulating substrates. The flexible insulating substrates are aligned in an arrangement direction such that the thermoelectric elements are arranged to form a thermoelectric conversion structure. The thermally conductive member is positioned relative to the flexible insulating substrates and configured to apply pressure thereto in the arrangement direction. The applied pressure maintains thermal contact between the thermoelectric elements, the flexible insulating substrates, and the thermally conductive member while accommodating dimensional variation and deformation of the module.

### Independent Apparatus Claim

1. **A thermoelectric conversion module comprising:**

   a plurality of flexible insulating substrates aligned in an arrangement direction;

   a plurality of thermoelectric elements, each of the thermoelectric elements being a P-type thermoelectric element or an N-type thermoelectric element and being formed on a corresponding one of the plurality of flexible insulating substrates;

   a plurality of conductive portions electrically connecting at least some of the thermoelectric elements; and

   a thermally conductive member disposed adjacent to the plurality of flexible insulating substrates and configured to apply pressure to the plurality of flexible insulating substrates in the arrangement direction.

### Dependent Claims

2. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the plurality of thermoelectric elements includes at least one P-type thermoelectric element and at least one N-type thermoelectric element.

3. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 2, wherein the P-type thermoelectric element and the N-type thermoelectric element are electrically connected in series.

4. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the flexible insulating substrates are arranged at intervals in the arrangement direction.

5. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein each flexible insulating substrate includes a first principal surface on which the corresponding thermoelectric element is formed and a second principal surface opposite the first principal surface.

6. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the thermally conductive member directly contacts at least one of the flexible insulating substrates.

7. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, further comprising a thermally conductive intermediate layer disposed between the thermally conductive member and at least one of the flexible insulating substrates.

8. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the thermally conductive member includes a first thermally conductive member and a second thermally conductive member, and the plurality of flexible insulating substrates is disposed between the first thermally conductive member and the second thermally conductive member in the arrangement direction.

9. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 8, wherein at least one of the first thermally conductive member or the second thermally conductive member is biased toward the plurality of flexible insulating substrates.

10. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 9, further comprising a biasing member configured to generate a compressive force between the first thermally conductive member and the second thermally conductive member.

11. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the pressure applied by the thermally conductive member elastically deforms at least a portion of one or more of the flexible insulating substrates.

12. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the thermally conductive member is configured to transfer heat between an external heat source or heat sink and the plurality of thermoelectric elements.

13. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the thermally conductive member comprises a metal, a ceramic, a graphite-containing material, or a combination thereof.

14. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the flexible insulating substrates comprise a polymer film.

15. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 14, wherein the polymer film comprises polyimide.

16. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the conductive portions are formed on the flexible insulating substrates.

17. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein adjacent flexible insulating substrates are electrically interconnected such that the plurality of thermoelectric elements forms a series circuit having first and second output terminals.

18. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the thermally conductive member applies substantially uniform pressure across the plurality of flexible insulating substrates.

19. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, further comprising an insulating, thermally conductive layer electrically isolating the thermally conductive member from the conductive portions.

20. The thermoelectric conversion module according to claim 1, wherein the flexible insulating substrates are aligned such that respective thermoelectric elements overlap one another as viewed in the arrangement direction.

### Method Claim

21. **A method of manufacturing a thermoelectric conversion module, the method comprising:**

   forming a P-type thermoelectric element or an N-type thermoelectric element on each of a plurality of flexible insulating substrates;

   aligning the plurality of flexible insulating substrates in an arrangement direction;

   electrically connecting at least some of the thermoelectric elements; and

   positioning a thermally conductive member relative to the plurality of flexible insulating substrates such that the thermally conductive member applies pressure to the plurality of flexible insulating substrates in the arrangement direction.

22. The method according to claim 21, further comprising disposing the plurality of flexible insulating substrates between first and second thermally conductive members and urging at least one of the first and second thermally conductive members toward the other.

23. The method according to claim 21, wherein applying the pressure causes elastic deformation of at least one of the flexible insulating substrates and increases thermal contact between the thermally conductive member and the thermoelectric elements.

### Specification-Style Embodiment

In one embodiment, a thermoelectric conversion module includes a plurality of flexible insulating substrates arranged in a predetermined arrangement direction. One or more P-type thermoelectric elements and/or one or more N-type thermoelectric elements are formed on respective flexible insulating substrates. Conductive patterns provided on the substrates electrically connect the thermoelectric elements in series, in parallel, or in a series-parallel configuration. A thermally conductive member is disposed at an end of, or around, the aligned flexible insulating substrates and applies a compressive load in the arrangement direction. The compressive load maintains the substrates and the thermoelectric elements in thermally coupled relation, suppresses formation of gaps attributable to manufacturing tolerances or thermal deformation, and facilitates heat transfer through the thermoelectric conversion module. The flexibility of the insulating substrates permits the substrates to conform to adjacent surfaces under the applied load, thereby reducing thermal contact resistance.
